correctness.rationale: For even d>=4, nondegenerate β and Q(0)=0, pure qubit graph-state bipartition across affine flat A=a+U, graph-state Schmidt entropy is binary cross-adjacency rank r. On k<=d-2 flats the complement affinely spans F2^d; row differences D_u(z)=β(u,z)+Q(u)+β(u,a) produce k dimensions and, precisely for nonisotropic U, the constant direction. The first row Q(a+z) cannot be affine-linear on the complement because any nondegenerate quadratic plus affine linear term has support at least 2^{d-1}-2^{d/2-1}>2^{d-2}. Thus r=k+1 or k+2. On hyperplanes, β restricted to U has 1-dimensional radical, difference-row span has dimension d-1 including constants, and the nonlinear row yields r=d. Finite independent row-reduction examples in dimension 4 agree with formula; argument handles every k, affine offset and quadratic refinement. Flat Schmidt spectrum follows from reduced-state cosets of kernel of cross matrix.
